chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from 'Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):

Regarding a man who prayed facing away from the Qibla, and he realized this while still in prayer before completing it: He said, 'If he was facing somewhere between East and West, let him turn his face to the Qibla when he realizes. And if he was facing directly behind the Qibla, let him break off the prayer, then turn his face to the Qibla, then restart the prayer.'
The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'And if he forgot the Opening Takbir intentionally or by mistake, he must repeat the prayer.'

key_terms.الْقِبْلَة: The direction of prayer towards the Kaaba in Mecca
key_terms.تَكْبِيرَةَ الِافْتِتَاحِ: The Opening Takbir (saying 'Allahu Akbar' to begin prayer)
key_terms.دُبُرِ الْقِبْلَة: Directly behind the Qibla (facing away from it)

ai.seo_question: What should a Muslim do if they realize they were praying in the wrong direction during their prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* details the fiqh of Qibla orientation, distinguishing between minor deviations where the prayer continues, and major misalignment requiring a restart. The inclusion of Shaykh al-Tusi’s note on the Opening Takbir (*Takbirat al-Ihtiram*) highlights the rigorous standards of Shia jurisprudence regarding the validity of prayer components. This ruling underscores the principle that while flexibility exists for unintentional errors, the structural integrity of the prayer must be maintained through correct orientation and recitation.
